title: The conic discriminant is invariant under a rotation of the plane
statement: A conic on the real plane is the six-coefficient datum (A,B,C,D,E,F) whose zero set is the points where A x^2 + B x y + C y^2 + D x + E y + F ~ 0. A rotation by the pair (c,s) with c^2 + s^2 ~ 1 acts on that datum by CPoint.Conic.rotate, and the discriminant B^2 - 4AC of the rotated conic is CReal.Equiv to the discriminant of the original. The unconditional form, proved first and stated separately as CPoint.Conic.discriminant_rotate, carries no hypothesis at all: the discriminant picks up exactly the factor (c^2 + s^2)^2 for EVERY (c,s), because the linear map behind the action has determinant c^2 + s^2 and the discriminant is -4 det Q for the quadratic-part matrix Q, which transforms as M^T Q M. The reflection CPoint.Conic.reflect gets the SAME factor -- its determinant is -(c^2 + s^2) and the discriminant sees only the square -- so orientation reversal is invisible to the classification, which is the correct answer since a reflection does not turn an ellipse into a hyperbola. A translation needs no hypothesis at all and its discriminant law is proved by CReal.Equiv.refl, because a translation copies A, B and C unchanged.

formal.statement: theorem CPoint.Conic.discriminant_rotate_unit : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal.Equiv (CReal.add (CReal.mul x0 x0) (CReal.mul x1 x1)) CReal.one) -> ((x3 : CPoint.Conic) -> CReal.Equiv (CPoint.Conic.discriminant (CPoint.Conic.rotate x0 x1 x3)) (CPoint.Conic.discriminant x3)))))

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the three classifying predicates are EXHAUSTIVE: there is no trichotomy theorem here and there cannot be one, because deciding the sign of a general constructive real is not constructive and CReal.lt carries a rational gap as data. What is proved instead is that the three are pairwise exclusive (CPoint.Conic.not_ellipse_and_parabola and its two siblings) and that each is inhabited by a named instance. It also does not say every isometry of the plane preserves the classification -- only the three GENERATORS translate/rotate/reflect are covered, one theorem each per predicate (nine in all); the classification theorem that every isometry is a rotation-or-reflection after a translation is not in tree, and creal_point/isometry.rs sizes it at four sub-shelves.
